verdict: Broadly usable coverage with observable outcomes, but it needs revision before serving as a precise sampling curriculum because several leaves mix weakly transferable capabilities, the hierarchy expresses almost no learning progression, and important boundaries fail on the supplied tasks.
findings: Coverage is strong at the guidepost level: the six roots correspond to all six C14 guideposts, and the discovery tasks have plausible destinations (t009-t010 under discrete enumeration, t011-t012 under exact computation, t025 under combinatorial enumeration, t026 under structural proof, and t027-t028 under geometric deduction or optimization). This small discovery sample is evidence of represented capabilities, not proof that the subject is complete.

Most outcomes are observable and the paired probes are substantive: for example, statistical inference asks for derivation and comparison of estimators or tests, while its two probes exercise estimation and hypothesis testing. The includes and excludes usually separate adjacent leaves better than topic labels alone would.

The discrete-enumeration leaf is too heterogeneous for reliable sampling or evaluation. Exact prime counting in t009-t010 is primarily sieve or primality-testing work, while the digit-order count in t025 uses combinatorial case analysis; success on either is weak evidence of success on the other. Separate integer/divisibility enumeration from finite combinatorial enumeration, or define a common counting procedure narrow enough to predict transfer.

The discrete-enumeration outcome says counts are obtained without exhaustive listing, but its own prime-count probe asks for systematic elimination of composites and t009-t010 request exact counts over large arbitrary intervals. Those tasks naturally require enumerating or sieving candidates, so the stated boundary excludes a central observed behavior. The outcome should admit systematic finite algorithms and distinguish them from naive manual listing.

The boundary between geometric deduction and optimization solution/certification is unresolved for t028. Geometric deduction explicitly includes extremal configurations, while optimization covers finding and certifying optima; neither exclusion determines where an intrinsically geometric maximum-circle problem belongs. State whether the decisive behavior is deriving the geometric feasible family or optimizing and certifying within an already derived model.

All prerequisite lists are empty, so the hierarchy is a taxonomy rather than a learnable progression. At minimum, derivations in statistical inference depend on probability-model operations, and system verification depends on logical formulation and deduction. If those dependencies are intentionally assumed background rather than trained stages, say so; otherwise add only the prerequisite edges whose absence prevents partial success.

The six internal nodes duplicate their descendants as task-generation targets. For example, the arithmetic root probes symbolic solving and finite counting, and the analysis root probes continuous analysis and geometry, without training a distinct combined behavior. Treat roots as organizational nodes, or give them synthesis outcomes that cannot be sampled from a single child; otherwise 20 sampled sections overstate the useful size of the curriculum.

Several broad leaves warrant a transfer check before further splitting: symbolic solving spans equation manipulation and recurrence solving, and continuous analysis spans limits, differentiation, integration, inequalities, and asymptotics. Their probes demonstrate variety but do not establish that success on one representative task predicts the rest. Split only where held-out mapping or performance evidence confirms this weak transfer.

The two-probe generation contract is otherwise met throughout: instructions are executable, differ in substance, and generally test the claimed operation rather than an answer format or data source. The prime-count boundary conflict and parent-child duplication are the material exceptions, not a pervasive probe-quality failure.
rubric_changes: Specify whether internal hierarchy nodes are eligible generation targets. If they are, require an outcome and probes behaviorally distinct from every child; if they are organizational only, apply the generation-probe and sampling-granularity criteria to leaves.
